selection.reason: RC39 proved a 2f+1 exact-report boundary while explicitly excluding analogue uncertainty, missing reports, and structured common causes. With no HIL hardware available, the highest-information next step is to determine when uncertainty alone merges event counts, how omission changes the witness lower bound, and which independently verifiable safeguards block every modeled false-certificate cut set without confusing refusal with recovery.

researchQuestion: For physical event counts separated by one unit, what interval width and active-witness quorum uniquely identify count under f arbitrary reports and m omissions, and what minimum safeguard hitting set blocks structured common-cause paths to false acceptance?
factsAtSeal: JCGM 106:2012 treats conformity as a decision under measurement uncertainty and explains that guard bands can limit incorrect-decision risk near tolerance boundaries.

JCGM's current publication list includes GUM-5:2026 examples and a 2026 amendment on nonlinearity, confirming that uncertainty propagation and decision rules remain active metrology work rather than a solved implementation detail.

Marzullo's 1990 primary study models continuous-valued sensor failures, modifies specifications to accommodate sensor uncertainty, and analyzes attainable accuracy under a hierarchy of failure models.

The NASA Fault Tree Handbook defines a minimal cut set as the smallest basic-event combination producing a top event and warns that common characteristics in a cut set reveal dependent or common-cause vulnerability.

NRC NUREG/CR-7007 distinguishes diversity across different technologies, different approaches within digital technology, and different architectures within one technology; merely counting nominally separate channels does not establish enough diversity.
RC39's official RATS, TPM, OPC UA, NIST, NASA, and NRC sources remain applicable to freshness, component binding, transport integrity, calibration, and common-cause boundaries.
No calibrated interval sensor, physical actuator, HIL device, independent power or clock domain, physical event, or empirical fault frequency is available in this workspace.

hypotheses.claim: When every healthy interval is narrower than the spacing between adjacent event counts, exact identification under at most f arbitrary interval reports and m missing reports is possible exactly when n is at least 2f+m+1.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: The complete n=1..6, f=0..2, m=0..2 grid at radius 0.25 will have zero observation collisions iff n>=2f+m+1; in particular n=3,f=1,m=1 will collide while n=4,f=1,m=1 will not.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any grid cell differs from the formula, the three-witness omission case identifies, or the four-witness omission case collides.

hypotheses.claim: Witness count alone can recover exact event count even when a healthy measurement interval spans adjacent count values.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: With count spacing one, a radius strictly below one will isolate the generating count in the finite report library, while radius one will admit one visible interval containing at least two truths even with n=1,f=0,m=0.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The radius-one fault-free case remains identifiable or a radius below one collides in the same no-fault design.

hypotheses.claim: A minimum set of independently verifiable safeguards can block every structured minimal cut set leading to false exact-certificate acceptance.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: The frozen seven-cut, eight-safeguard incidence structure will have minimum hitting-set size five and exactly three minimum sets, each containing separate processing, epoch, identity, calibration, and one external physical veto modality.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The exact enumeration finds a smaller set, a different number of minimum sets, or a minimum set omits one of the four forced non-sensor controls or lacks an external physical veto.

hypotheses.claim: One outside-domain veto witness both detects a false operational consensus and recovers the exact physical event count.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: For truth one with operational reports [0,0,0] and outside report one, naive plurality returns the wrong zero while a safe veto policy returns inconclusive; exact recovery still requires its own active quorum.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The outside report makes majority recovery correct without additional assumptions or the veto policy accepts the operational zero.

hypotheses.claim: Missing physical evidence can be ignored without changing exact-identification guarantees.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: An all-missing allowed observation will be compatible with every truth; each additional allowed omission raises the necessary witness count by one in the narrow-interval bound.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: An allowed all-missing observation identifies one truth or the grid is independent of m.

causalChain.inputAndAllowedAssumptions: Event counts {0,1,2}, unit count spacing, a finite interval library, arbitrary-report budget f, omission budget m, and an explicit structured fault tree.
causalChain.bottleneck: Healthy uncertainty may cover adjacent counts, missingness may erase the honest majority, and a shared fault can corrupt every operational channel or bind a correct value to the wrong event.
causalChain.bridgeLemma: For the frozen interval library with radius below count spacing, any alternative truth needs f arbitrary reports plus more honest support than the remaining n-f-m channels; singleton identification is therefore expected exactly at n>=2f+m+1.
causalChain.independentAdjudicand: Truth-set cardinality for each visible interval vector plus exact enumeration of safeguard subsets hitting every frozen minimal cut set.
causalChain.finalCriterion: Exact recovery requires singleton interval classes under the declared f,m budget; safe refusal requires every modeled false-acceptance cut set to be hit, and the two claims must never be merged.

intervalModel.healthyReportRule: Any library interval containing the true count is admissible.
intervalModel.arbitraryReportRule: An arbitrary witness may emit any interval in the library.
intervalModel.missingReportRule: A missing witness emits null and consumes the omission budget.
intervalModel.stopRule: Stop without a scientific verdict if JavaScript and independent Python differ on any cell's world, observation, collision, or identification count, any radius-sweep result, or any minimum hitting set. Preserve the first outputs before amending code.

structuredFaultTree.topEvent: accept a false exact physical-event certificate
structuredFaultTree.semanticBoundary: Hitting one basic event in each minimal cut set prevents the modeled top event through safe refusal. It does not estimate cut-set probabilities, prove safeguard effectiveness, or provide an exact-recovery quorum.

criteria: C1 narrow interval grid matches n>=2f+m+1
C2 n=3 tolerates f=1 with m=0
C3 n=3 fails with f=1 and m=1
C4 n=4 tolerates f=1 and m=1
C5 radii below count spacing identify without faults
C6 radius at count spacing collides without faults
C7 an all-missing allowed observation is ambiguous
C8 minimum safeguard hitting set has size five
C9 exactly three minimum safeguard sets exist
C10 every minimum set includes four forced non-sensor controls
C11 every minimum set includes one external physical veto
C12 every reported minimum set is inclusion-minimal
C13 an external veto refuses while naive plurality is wrong
C14 no physical result is claimed

uncertaintyBudget.measurement: Interval radii are designed values, not calibrated coverage intervals. No distribution, coverage probability, bias, drift, hysteresis, latency, or environmental transfer is measured.
uncertaintyBudget.missingness: Missing reports are bounded adversarially; the model does not estimate whether field missingness is random, condition-dependent, or attacker-induced.
uncertaintyBudget.faultTree: The seven minimal cut sets are a prospective design grammar, not an empirical completeness claim or frequency model. Unknown common causes may remain outside the tree.
uncertaintyBudget.safeguards: A coverage edge means a safeguard is designed to block one basic fault; effectiveness requires a future independent artifact and is not proven by enumeration.
uncertaintyBudget.externalValidity: The n>=2f+m+1 result applies to scalar unit-spaced counts and the frozen interval library, not arbitrary continuous dynamics or correlated analogue errors.
uncertaintyBudget.decision: The model separates safe refusal from exact recovery; an inconclusive veto is not counted as a recovered event count.
